new.n: "Wolf River Jack": tin cans of money rumored buried by his shack near Lily
new.pl: Near Lily (Langlade Co.); his shack on the Wolf River about 25 mi NE of Antigo is not located
new.v: Rumored tin cans of money (no amount)
new.st: A hermit known as "Wolf River Jack" (John Smith; the FBI later named him William Warnick Jr.) lived alone in a shack on the Wolf River about 25 mi NE of Antigo and was found dead near it on 9 Jun 1939, killed by a blow to the head. Police believed his killer had heard he hid his money in tin cans buried in the earth; "legend was that he had a fortune buried in the woods." The two robbers who killed him had hoped to find the fortune and found nothing; both pleaded guilty. No amount and no proof it existed. The pin marks Lily, not the shack.
new.t: Near Lily; shack not located (likely a squatter shack on the river). Story only until the shack is placed. River frontage may be public: check the rules.
src: Marshfield News-Herald, 15 Jun 1939, p. 2 (AP, Antigo; newspapers.com 267364583)
